Senses.Explanation: Literally, ‘strike or clap the palms.’ The gesture occurs 746 times in 231 allowlisted texts, commonly as a visible turn in a public exchange. It may stand alone (‘clapped three times’), accompany departure, a shout, or a blow, or join laughter: ‘clapped his hands and laughed loudly’ occurs 98 times in 60 texts. The record does not assign one fixed attitude to it. One master claps and laughs before saying an answer is ‘not worth half a cent’; another monk claps once after shouting; Xiyuan claps three times when asked why he bathes without an attendant. Caoshan later explicitly calls the action ‘hand-clapping’ and distinguishes Xiyuan’s use from the same physical action elsewhere. In the Shuilao case, Shuilao rises after Mazu kicks him, claps and laughs, and speaks; later records repeatedly cite that sequence. Zen bends an ordinary gesture by making it an answer, rejoinder, appraisal, or recorded public-interview move, while the surrounding words—not the gesture alone—establish whether a given occurrence is laughter, challenge, celebration, or dismissal.
Senses.Note: Family check: “clap the hands” (撫掌), “hand-clapping” (拍手撫掌), “clap and laugh loudly” (撫掌大笑), “clap once” (撫掌一下), and “clap three times” (撫掌三下) all denote the same physical action. They differ in accompanying speech and count, not referent, so they remain one sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 乃撫掌作舞，大笑云：「菩薩子喫飯來！」後有僧舉問長慶：「古人撫掌大笑，意作摩生？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Ancestor Hall Collection (祖堂集): Jinniu Heshang brings food before the hall, claps his hands, dances, laughs, and calls the bodhisattva-children to eat.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：和尚不使沙彌童行，何得自燒？師撫掌三下。後僧舉似曹山，山云：一等是箇拍手撫掌，就中西園奇怪，俱胝一指頭禪，蓋謂承當處不諦當。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linked Lamps Compendium (聯燈會要): inside Xiyuan Tancang's explicitly headed section, Xiyuan Tancang responds to the monk's challenge about heating his own bath by clapping his hands three times.

Occurrences.Kwic: 主指曰：春雨霖霖。師撫掌大笑曰：不直半分錢。主便喝，師曰：者瞎漢向道不直半分錢，又惡發作什麼？主撫掌一下，師曰：且坐喫茶。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): in Yangqi Fanghui's section, Yangqi Fanghui is the first exact actor at the stored occurrence: after the visiting Daowu offering-master points and says 'the spring rain pours down,' Yangqi claps his hands, laughs, and appraises the answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 大師欄胷與一踏踏倒，當下大悟，起來撫掌大笑云：也大奇！也大奇！百千法門，無量妙義，只向一毫頭上識得根源去。便作禮。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linked Lamps Compendium (聯燈會要): inside Shuilao Heshang's explicitly headed case, Shuilao is knocked down by Mazu Daoyi, awakens, rises clapping his hands, and laughs while declaring the many teaching gates known at one point.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧以手面前一劃師云是何言欵僧便喝師云作甚麼僧撫掌一下便打師云瞎漢乱做作麼以坐具真打出法堂
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄): in Ciming Chuyuan's record, an unnamed monk makes the palm-clapping action; Ciming rebukes and drives him from the hall. The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel-passage search do not name the unnamed monk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂撫掌大笑良久曰大眾笑箇什麼山僧笑古往今來一切人有瞥地有不瞥地
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Ancient Worthies (古尊宿語錄): inside his Longmen upper-hall record, Foyan Qingyuan claps his hands, laughs loudly, pauses, and asks the assembly what they think he is laughing at.
